key_insight: PackForcing lets models trained on short video clips generate coherent long videos by managing history with a three-partition KV-cache, avoiding linear cache growth and temporal repetition while enabling long-context inference.
problem_solved: Autoregressive video diffusion models struggle with intractable linear KV-cache growth, temporal repetition, and compounding errors when scaling to long-video generation and long-context inference.
method: Three-partition KV-cache: split history into Sink tokens (persistent, preserved memory), Pack tokens (condensed summaries of older content), and Window tokens (detailed recent context) to limit unbounded cache growth.

Train on short videos but apply a packing/summarization strategy at sampling time (PackForcing) so the model reuses compacted history to generate long sequences without needing full linear KV expansion.
Inference-level protocol that periodically compresses older context into Pack tokens and maintains fidelity in Window tokens, reducing repetition and compounding errors for long-rollout sampling.
impact: Practitioners can use short-video training budgets to produce long, coherent video outputs with much lower memory and compute overhead, enabling scalable long-context video generation and downstream tasks that require extended temporal reasoning.

paper_title: PackForcing: Short Video Training Suffices for Long Video Sampling and Long Context Inference
paper_authors: Xiaofeng Mao, Shaohao Rui, Kaining Ying, Bo Zheng, Chuanhao Li
